examples: Let us have a meal together.
Today the meal is really tasty.
저는 보통 일곱 시에 식사를 해요.
I usually have a meal at seven.
nuance: 식사 is a more formal word for a meal than 밥, so it sounds polite and respectful. 식사하셨어요? is a common warm greeting to older people.
mistakes: Using 식사 casually with close friends like 밥

examples: I add a little salt to the soup.
This food has too much salt.
nuance: 소금 is plain table salt and is the most basic seasoning in any kitchen. Koreans often say 싱거워요 when food needs more 소금 to taste fuller.
mistakes: Confusing 소금 salt with 설탕 sugar

usage: I add a lot of sugar
examples: I add sugar to the coffee.
I do not eat much sugar.
This bread has too much sugar.
nuance: 설탕 is white refined sugar used to make food or drinks sweet. Many Korean dishes use a little 설탕 to balance salty and spicy flavors.
mistakes: Mixing up 설탕 sugar with 소금 salt

examples: I eat dumplings dipped in soy sauce.
This soy sauce is a bit salty.
I add a little soy sauce to the dish.
nuance: 간장 is dark salty soy sauce used widely in Korean cooking and as a dip. It gives a deep savory flavor that salt alone cannot.
mistakes: Saying 간장 is sweet when it is salty

examples: I add chili paste to bibimbap.
This chili paste is really spicy.
I mix rice with chili paste and eat.
nuance: 고추장 is thick red fermented chili paste that is both spicy and slightly sweet. It is essential for dishes like bibimbap and many spicy stews.
mistakes: Treating 고추장 as the same thing as 된장

examples: Mom makes stew with soybean paste.
This soybean paste is a bit salty.
I dissolve soybean paste in the soup.
nuance: 된장 is brown fermented soybean paste with a deep savory and salty taste. It is the base of 된장찌개, a very common everyday Korean stew.
mistakes: Confusing 된장 paste with red 고추장 paste

examples: I add a little vinegar to cold noodles.
I mix vinegar into the salad.
nuance: 식초 is sour vinegar used to add a fresh tangy taste to food. Koreans often add a little 식초 to cold noodles and pickled side dishes.
mistakes: Expecting 식초 to taste sweet rather than sour

examples: I sprinkle pepper on the meat.
nuance: 후추 is ground black pepper that adds a sharp warm spiciness to food. It is different from 고추 chili and is usually sprinkled on at the end.
mistakes: Confusing 후추 black pepper with 고추 chili pepper

examples: Mom makes the seasoning for the meat.
This seasoning is a bit spicy.
I marinate the chicken in seasoning.
nuance: 양념 is a mix of seasonings like soy sauce, garlic, and sugar used to flavor food. 양념 chicken means chicken coated in a sweet and spicy sauce.
mistakes: Thinking 양념 means only one single spice

examples: I drink up all the ramyeon broth.
nuance: 국물 is the liquid part of a soup or stew, separate from the solid pieces. Koreans say a hot 국물 is 시원해요, meaning it feels refreshing inside.
mistakes: Translating 시원한 국물 as cold instead of refreshing

examples: I mix the flour with water.
nuance: 밀가루 is wheat flour used to make bread, noodles, and many fried foods. 밀가루 음식 refers to flour-based dishes like noodles and dumplings.
mistakes: Using 밀가루 for cooked rice powder products

usage: I add a little sesame oil
examples: I add sesame oil to bibimbap.
This dish smells nicely of sesame oil.
I add a little sesame oil to the rice.
nuance: 참기름 is fragrant sesame oil added at the end of cooking for a rich nutty aroma. Koreans describe its warm toasty flavor with the word 고소해요.
mistakes: Using 참기름 for frying instead of finishing
